items.prompt: What is the common name for many flowering ceroid cacti that bloom at night?

options.label: Night-blooming cereus
options.feedback: Correct. Night-blooming cereus is the common name for many cacti in the ceroid group that open their flowers after dark.

options.label: Queen of the night
options.feedback: Queen of the night is one of the other names for some of these cacti, but it is not the common name for the group as a whole.

options.label: Princess of the night
options.feedback: Princess of the night is an alternate name used for one or more of these cacti, not the collective common name.

options.label: Dama de noche
options.feedback: Dama de noche is another name for some night-blooming cereus, but the group's common name is different.

items.ok_line: Night-blooming cereus is the right term.
items.ko_line: That is one of the other names, not the common one.
items.exp_text: The common name for these cacti is night-blooming cereus, because they belong to the ceroid group and their flowers open at night.

items.prompt: How long does a single flower of Selenicereus grandiflorus stay open?

options.label: Only one night
options.feedback: Correct. Each flower of Selenicereus grandiflorus blooms for a single night and then is done.

options.label: A whole week
options.feedback: A week is far too long; these flowers open only at night and wilt by dawn.

options.label: Several nights in a row
options.feedback: No, the flower does not reopen; it lasts just one night.

options.label: A full day and night
options.feedback: The flower opens after nightfall and wilts by dawn, so it does not stay through a full day.

items.ok_line: The flower opens once and fades by dawn.
items.ko_line: The bloom lasts only a single night.
items.exp_text: Each flower of this species opens for just one night, which is why the plant is called night-blooming cereus.

items.prompt: What color are the flowers of night-blooming cereus almost always?

options.label: Bright yellow
options.feedback: Yellow is not typical; these flowers are almost always white or very pale.

options.label: White or very pale shades
options.feedback: Correct. Night-blooming cereus flowers are almost always white or very pale in color.

options.label: Deep red
options.feedback: Red is not mentioned; the flowers are pale rather than vivid.

options.label: Dark purple
options.feedback: Dark purple would be the opposite of the pale shades these flowers show.

items.ok_line: White or pale is the usual color.
items.ko_line: These flowers are not brightly colored.
items.exp_text: Night-blooming cereus flowers are almost always white or very pale shades of other colors, which helps them be seen by night pollinators.

items.prompt: When do most night-blooming cereus flowers open?

options.label: At noon
options.feedback: Noon is daytime; these flowers open after nightfall.

options.label: Just before sunrise
options.feedback: Before sunrise is still dark, but the flowers open after nightfall, typically later in the evening.

options.label: After nightfall
options.feedback: Correct. Most of the flowers open after nightfall.

options.label: During the afternoon
options.feedback: Afternoon is daylight, and these flowers wait for the dark.

items.ko_line: These flowers do not open in daylight.
items.exp_text: Most night-blooming cereus flowers open after nightfall and are wilting by dawn, so they are active only in the dark.

items.prompt: What happens to a night-blooming cereus flower by dawn?

options.label: It opens wider
options.feedback: Opening wider is not what happens; the flower is closing and wilting.

options.label: It turns blue
options.feedback: Color change is not described; the flower simply wilts.

options.label: It drops its petals
options.feedback: Dropping petals is not stated; the flower wilts but does not necessarily shed petals.

options.label: It is wilting
options.feedback: Correct. By dawn, most of these flowers are wilting.

items.ok_line: The flower wilts as morning comes.
items.ko_line: It does not stay fresh; it wilts.
items.exp_text: Most night-blooming cereus flowers are wilting by dawn, which is why they are so short-lived.

items.prompt: Which genus includes the cactus most frequently cultivated outdoors and the main source of dragon fruit?

options.label: Hylocereus
options.feedback: Correct. Hylocereus undatus is the most frequently cultivated outdoors and is the main source of dragon fruit.

options.label: Selenicereus
options.feedback: Selenicereus is another night-blooming cereus, but it is not the main source of dragon fruit.

options.label: Echinopsis
options.feedback: Echinopsis includes San Pedro cactus, not the main dragon fruit source.

options.label: Epiphyllum
options.feedback: Epiphyllum is popular as a houseplant, not the main outdoor cultivated dragon fruit source.

items.ko_line: That genus is not the main dragon fruit producer.
items.exp_text: Hylocereus undatus is the most frequently cultivated outdoors and is the main source of the commercial fruit crop, dragon fruit.

items.prompt: Which of these is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus, often grown as an indoor houseplant?

options.label: Hylocereus undatus
options.feedback: Hylocereus undatus is cultivated outdoors, not primarily as an indoor houseplant.

options.label: Epiphyllum oxypetalum
options.feedback: Correct. Epiphyllum oxypetalum, also called gooseneck cactus, is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus and is grown indoors worldwide.

options.label: Selenicereus grandiflorus
options.feedback: Selenicereus grandiflorus is known for single-night blooms, but it is not the most popular cultivated one.

options.label: Peniocereus greggii
options.feedback: Peniocereus greggii is a desert plant that is infrequently cultivated.

items.ko_line: That cactus is not the most cultivated indoors.
items.exp_text: Epiphyllum oxypetalum, known as gooseneck cactus, is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus and is grown as an indoor houseplant worldwide.

items.prompt: What shape do the plants that bear night-blooming cereus flowers most frequently have?

options.label: Short and round like a ball
options.feedback: A round ball shape is not the typical form; most are climbers.

options.label: Thin-stemmed climbers
options.feedback: Correct. More frequently, the plants are thin-stemmed climbers.

options.label: Tall and flat like a leaf
options.feedback: Flat leaf-like stems are not the typical shape; climbers are more common.

options.label: Low and spreading like a mat
options.feedback: A mat-like growth is not described; they are climbers or tall columns.

items.ko_line: The usual shape is a thin-stemmed climber.
items.exp_text: While some are tall and columnar, more frequently the plants are thin-stemmed climbers.

options.label: A common name for many flowering cacti that bloom at night
options.feedback: Correct. It is a common name covering many different ceroid cacti that share the habit of opening at night.

options.label: A single species of cactus found only in deserts
options.feedback: Not that. Night-blooming cereus is a common name for many species, not one, and they are not all desert plants.

options.label: A type of flower that stays open for several nights
options.feedback: No. Most night-blooming cereus flowers open for just one night, and some for only part of it.

options.label: A plant that blooms during the day instead of at night
options.feedback: The name says otherwise. These cacti bloom at night, not during the day.

items.ok_line: It is a shared name for many night-blooming cacti.
items.ko_line: Remember it covers many species, not one.
items.exp_text: Night-blooming cereus is a common name applied to many flowering ceroid cacti that bloom at night. The name is not a single species but a label for a group of cacti sharing this habit.

items.prompt: Which cactus is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus?

options.label: Selenicereus grandiflorus
options.feedback: Not that. Although it is a night-blooming cereus, it is not the most popular one grown; Epiphyllum oxypetalum holds that place.

options.label: Hylocereus undatus
options.feedback: No. That one is often grown outdoors for its fruit, but the most popular cultivated for its flowers is Epiphyllum oxypetalum.

options.label: Epiphyllum oxypetalum
options.feedback: Correct. Epiphyllum oxypetalum, also called gooseneck cactus, is the most popular cultivated night-blooming cereus and is grown as a houseplant worldwide.

options.label: Peniocereus greggii
options.feedback: No. That desert cactus is infrequently cultivated, not the most popular one.

items.ok_line: Epiphyllum oxypetalum is the top choice among growers.
items.ko_line: It is Epiphyllum oxypetalum, not the others.
items.exp_text: Among night-blooming cereus, Epiphyllum oxypetalum is the most popular cultivated one. It is grown as an indoor houseplant throughout the world because it is relatively easy to keep.
